questions.question: Trade routes are the pathways connecting settlements, territories and landscapes.
questions.explanation: True. At the macro level, trade routes are the pathways that connect settlements, territories and landscapes.

questions.question: The Silk Route and the ______ route were among the earliest and most extensive trade networks, linking Africa, Asia and Europe.
questions.explanation: The session pairs the overland Silk Route with the Indian Ocean spice route as the earliest, most extensive networks.

questions.question: Which description fits the spice route in the session?
questions.explanation: The silk route is the overland route across Asia; the spice route is the Indian Ocean route through India.
options: The overland route across Central Asia to Rome
The coastal route of the Harappans to Oman
The Indian Ocean route through India
The route along the Ganga to Tamralipti

questions.question: The overland route across Asia that carried goods between China and the West is called the:
questions.explanation: The session calls the overland route across Asia the silk route.

questions.question: Why were states keen on developing and controlling trade routes, according to the session?
questions.explanation: Routes were important landscape features in cultural interactions, and states wanted to improve connectivity and gain advantage.
options: To stop all foreign merchants entering
To avoid building any rest houses
To make caravans travel only at night
To improve connectivity and gain advantage from interactions

questions.question: How do the silk route and the spice route differ in the session?
questions.explanation: The silk route is overland across Asia; the spice route crosses the Indian Ocean through India.
options: Silk route: sea route to Africa; spice route: land route to China
Silk route: overland across Asia; spice route: Indian Ocean route through India
Silk route: Indian rivers only; spice route: Himalayan passes only
They are two names for the same overland road

questions.question: A kingdom builds roads, secures mountain passes and develops harbours so that merchants can travel easily and its own revenue grows. Which idea from the session does this show?
questions.explanation: The session says states were keen on developing and controlling routes or highways for connectivity and advantage.
options: Trade routes were only natural paths that no state influenced
States developed and controlled trade routes to improve connectivity and gain advantage
Only caravans, never states, benefited from routes
Routes mattered only for religious journeys

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The silk route and the spice route connected Africa, Asia and Europe.
Reason (R): The Silk Road spanned almost 7,000 miles.
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but the length of the Silk Road does not explain how the two networks connected the three continents.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

questions.question: India's strategic position, according to the session, lies on routes of communication between:
questions.explanation: India occupies a strategic position along routes of communication between East and West.

questions.question: According to the session, the Himalayas lie only to the north-west of India.
questions.explanation: False. The session places the Himalayas to the north-west, north and north-east, with gaps and passes that served as routes of communication.

questions.question: Which passes in the north-west are named in the session? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: The north-west passes named are Karakoram, Burzil, Lanak La and Zoji La. Thang La and Tulung La are in the north-east.

questions.question: Which of these passes is NOT among the north-eastern passes named in the session?
questions.explanation: The north-eastern passes named are Thang La, Tulung La, Dom La and Andra La. Zoji La is listed among the north-western passes.

questions.question: The passes in the Himalayas served as a means of communication between India and:
questions.explanation: The gaps and passes connected India with Central Asia, Tibet and China.

questions.question: Match each route or movement with its description.
questions.explanation: These come from the session's account of India's importance in the ancient trade network.
pairs: Tamralipti on the eastern seacoast to the Oxus region
Kausambi and Mathura with Ujjayini and Bharukachha
Gujarat and Makran coast to Oman, Bahrain and West Asia

questions.question: The Uttarapatha extended from Tamralipti (Tamluk) on the eastern seacoast up to the ______ region.
questions.explanation: The great northern route ran from Tamralipti up to the Oxus region.

questions.question: Tamralipti (Tamluk), the starting point of the Uttarapatha, lay on the:
questions.explanation: The session places Tamralipti on the eastern seacoast.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT named in the session as a city linked by the Uttarapatha?
questions.explanation: The Uttarapatha linked Champa, Pataliputra, Kasi, Kausambi, Mathura, Sakala, Taxila, Prushupura, Kapisa and Balkh. Muziris is a port-trade centre listed elsewhere.

questions.question: Another important route across the central Indian plateau linked Kausambi and Mathura with Ujjayini and:
questions.explanation: The central plateau route led to Bharukachha (Barygaza) on the west coast.

questions.question: The session says the Indian Ocean is at the centre of global maritime networks because it is encircled by:
questions.explanation: The Indian Ocean is encircled by the continents of Africa, Europe and Asia.

questions.question: Why did many ports and sheltered anchorages develop along the Indian coast, according to the session?
questions.explanation: Lagoons, lakes and other sheltered water bodies along the coast favoured the development of ports and sheltered anchorages.
options: Open, surf-battered beaches that attracted merchant fleets and ships
Lagoons, lakes and sheltered water bodies favoured ports and the plying of boats
Mountain passes that forced all trade to leave by sea
Royal orders that required every caravan to end at the coast

questions.question: The ______ were the earliest mariners, helped by the monsoon winds.
questions.explanation: The session says the Harappans were the earliest mariners, facilitated by the monsoon winds.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The Himalayan passes served as a means of communication between India and Central Asia, Tibet and China.
Reason (R): The Himalayas formed a complete barrier with no gaps or passes.
questions.explanation: A is true. R is false: the session notes a number of gaps and passes in the Himalayas that carried communication.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

questions.question: How does the Uttarapatha differ from the central plateau route?
questions.explanation: The Uttarapatha crossed the north from east coast to the Oxus; the central plateau route linked the Gangetic towns with the west-coast port.
options: Uttarapatha: Kausambi to Ujjayini; central route: Tamralipti to the Oxus region
Both routes ran only along the Makran coast, from Sutkagendor to Oman
Uttarapatha was a sea route to Barygaza; the central route a river route to Taxila
Uttarapatha: Tamralipti to the Oxus region; central route: Kausambi and Mathura to Ujjayini and Bharukachha

questions.question: A merchant at Kausambi wants to send goods to the west coast. Which route does the session describe for this?
questions.explanation: The central plateau route linked Kausambi and Mathura with Ujjayini and the west-coast port of Bharukachha.
options: The central plateau route via Ujjayini to Bharukachha
The Silk Road branch to Leh

questions.question: The Harappan coastal route linked Gujarat (Lothal and Dholavira) to the Makran coast at ______.
questions.explanation: The coastal route ran from the Gujarat sites of Lothal and Dholavira to Sutkagendor on the Makran coast.

questions.question: Which two Gujarat sites were joined to the Makran coast by the Harappan coastal route?
questions.explanation: Lothal and Dholavira were the Gujarat ends of the coastal route.

questions.question: The Harappan route between Sindh and South Baluchistan passed through the:
questions.explanation: Sindh and South Baluchistan were linked via the Kirthar mountains.

questions.question: Which regions did the Harappan route through the Cholistan tract connect?
questions.explanation: The Cholistan tract route linked Punjab, East Punjab and Rajasthan.

questions.question: Which raw materials were traded by the Harappans, according to the session? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Raw materials included shell, copper, gold, lead, zinc, alabaster, limestone, steatite and semi-precious stones. Wine and silk belong to later trade.

questions.question: Which of these are semi-precious stones named in the session's Harappan trade list?
questions.explanation: The session names carnelian, agate and jasper as semi-precious stones.

questions.question: The Harappan external trade route went via Iran and Afghanistan into West Asia and Central Asia.
questions.explanation: True. The external route ran through Iran and Afghanistan to West and Central Asia.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT described as an internal Harappan route?
questions.explanation: Pataliputra to Tamralipti is not a Harappan route; the Harappan internal routes included Sindh-Gujarat and Sindh-Baluchistan via Kachchh and Kathiawar.
options: Sindh and Baluchistan via Kachchh and Kathiawar
Coastal Sindh, Upper Sindh and the Central Indus plains

questions.question: Match each Harappan route with the regions it connected.
questions.explanation: These are four of the Harappan routes described in the session.
pairs: Lothal and Dholavira to the Makran coast

questions.question: A Harappan merchant has processed carnelian and wants to reach buyers in West Asia. Which route in the session fits?
questions.explanation: The Harappan external route went via Iran and Afghanistan into West and Central Asia.
options: The external route via Iran and Afghanistan
The Silk Road branch to Leh
The central plateau route to Bharukachha

questions.question: How do the Harappan internal routes differ from the external route?
questions.explanation: Internal routes connected Sindh, Baluchistan, Punjab, Rajasthan and Gujarat; the external route reached West and Central Asia.
options: Internal routes led onward to Rome; the external route stayed inside Sindh and Baluchistan
Both kinds of route linked only Gujarat and the Makran coast in the same way
Internal routes were sea routes; the external route was only a river route in Punjab
Internal routes linked regions of the Indus world; the external route led via Iran and Afghanistan to West and Central Asia

questions.question: The session says Harappan raw materials were obtained and then manufactured at:
questions.explanation: Raw materials such as shell, copper and steatite were obtained and manufactured at processing centres.

questions.question: What does the Anuradhapura excavation show, according to the session?
questions.explanation: Stratigraphical evidence at Anuradhapura shows Brahmi script came to Sri Lanka with Indian traders, probably in the 5th-4th century BC.
options: Roman coins reached Sri Lanka through Indian ports, probably in the 5th century AD
Sri Lankan traders founded the port of Tamralipti in the 4th century BC
Brahmi script was introduced in Sri Lanka by Indian traders, probably in the 5th-4th century BC
Kharoshti script was invented there and carried to India by Sri Lankan traders

questions.question: Brahmi and Kharoshti inscriptions (1st-5th century AD) found at Tamralipti and in West Bengal suggest that Bengal had trade contacts with:
questions.explanation: The inscriptions on pots, seals and plaques indicate trade contacts between Bengal and north-west India.

questions.question: Traders from the Gandhara and Oxus regions reached Mathura and the Gangetic valley by sea and then travelled overland to Southeast Asia.
questions.explanation: False. They came to Mathura and the Gangetic valley by the inland route and then voyaged to Southeast Asian countries.

questions.question: Where have Kharoshti-Brahmi or Kharoshti inscriptions been found, suggesting that script and language migrated with trade? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Inscriptions are reported from Bengal, Odisha, Thailand, Vietnam, Bali and Funan.

questions.question: What kind of evidence is called the best example for outlining contacts and routes between India, Southeast Asia and West Asia?
questions.explanation: Ceramic evidence, especially Indian-origin Rouletted ware, is found across the subcontinent, Southeast Asia and West Asia.
options: Ceramic evidence such as Rouletted ware

questions.question: Indian-origin ceramics called ______ ware are found across the subcontinent, Southeast Asia and West Asia.
questions.explanation: Rouletted ware is the ceramic evidence of contacts and routes.

questions.question: The excavations at Ban Don Ta Phet in Thailand suggest that India-Southeast Asia maritime contact is datable to the:
questions.explanation: Ban Don Ta Phet suggests contact as early as the 4th century BCE.

questions.question: According to the session, from which country did India mainly import high-bronze tin, needed for coinage?
questions.explanation: High-bronze tin, yellow like gold and needed for coinage, came mainly from Thailand.

questions.question: Which Southeast Asian region is named as the source of spices that fetched high profits?
questions.explanation: The session names the eastern Indonesian islands as the source of high-profit spices.

questions.question: What did the Chola naval expedition's trade involve, according to the session?
questions.explanation: Chola exports were pearls, pepper and textiles; imports were camphor, copper and tin.
options: Exports of horses and glass; imports of wine, lead and asphalt from Rome
Exports of wine and asphalt; imports of pepper, pearls and textiles
Exports of tin and camphor; imports of pearls, pepper and textiles
Exports of pearls, pepper and textiles; imports of camphor, copper and tin

questions.question: According to the session, in the early centuries CE mariners of India, Southeast Asia, the Red Sea, the Persian Gulf and the Mediterranean were strongly interlinked.
questions.explanation: True. Archaeological evidence points to a strong interlink among these regions.

questions.question: A scholar finds Kharoshti-Brahmi inscriptions on potsherds in Thailand and Vietnam. What does the session suggest this indicates?
questions.explanation: The findings suggest that the script and language migrated to overseas countries along with trade.
options: Script and language migrated overseas along with trade
The inscriptions were brought by Silk Road caravans only

questions.question: How do the Anuradhapura and Ban Don Ta Phet findings differ in what they show?
questions.explanation: Anuradhapura shows script spreading to Sri Lanka; Ban Don Ta Phet dates maritime contact between India and Southeast Asia.
options: Anuradhapura: Roman coins in Sri Lanka; Ban Don Ta Phet: Mauryan edicts in Thailand
Both sites show Silk Road caravans crossing the Karakoram into Kashmir
Anuradhapura: Brahmi script reaching Sri Lanka; Ban Don Ta Phet: early India-Southeast Asia contact
Anuradhapura: the Chola navy at sea; Ban Don Ta Phet: Harappan seals in Thailand

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Rouletted ware of Indian origin is found only within the Indian subcontinent.
Reason (R): Ceramic evidence is the best example for outlining the contacts and routes between peoples.
questions.explanation: A is false: Rouletted ware is found across the subcontinent, Southeast Asia and West Asia. R is true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

questions.question: Which of these is NOT listed as an export or import in the Chola expedition trade?
questions.explanation: The Chola list names pearls, pepper and textiles as exports and camphor, copper and tin as imports.

questions.question: A trader buys tin that is yellow like gold and needed for coinage, and sells Indian spices abroad. Which source and benefit does the session mention?
questions.explanation: The session names Thailand as the main source of high-bronze tin and the eastern Indonesian islands for profitable spices.
options: Tin from Thailand and high profits from spices of the eastern Indonesian islands
Tin from Egypt and high profits from horses bought in Arabia
Tin from Rome and high profits from wine sold in Southeast Asia
Tin from Persia and high profits from glass sold in the Indonesian islands

questions.question: Brahmi and Kharoshti inscriptions of the 1st-5th century AD were found on which objects at Tamralipti and in West Bengal?
questions.explanation: The inscriptions were found on pots, seals and plaques.

questions.question: The Anuradhapura excavation shows Indian traders introduced ______ script to Sri Lanka.
questions.explanation: Stratigraphical evidence at Anuradhapura shows the introduction of Brahmi script by traders of India.

questions.question: The session says the Chola naval expedition's exports included camphor, copper and tin.
questions.explanation: False. Exports were pearls, pepper and textiles; camphor, copper and tin were imports.

questions.question: Which statement about the archaeological evidence is NOT supported by the session?
questions.explanation: Rouletted ware is found across India, Southeast Asia and West Asia, not only in Rome.
options: Ban Don Ta Phet suggests 4th century BCE contact
Rouletted ware is found only in Rome
Anuradhapura shows Brahmi script reaching Sri Lanka
Inscriptions in Thailand suggest script migrated with trade

questions.question: A group of merchants travelling together for safety is called a:
questions.explanation: The session defines a caravan as a group of merchants travelling together for safety.

questions.question: Which pack animals are named for caravan trade? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: The session names camels, horses, bullocks and donkeys.

questions.question: Which caravan infrastructure is named? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Infrastructure along routes included inns or serais, wells and fortified outposts.

questions.question: The earliest Indian reference to a caravanserai is found in:
questions.explanation: The earliest reference is in the Delhi-Topra pillar edict No. 7, 3rd century BCE, under Ashoka.
options: The Periplus of the Erythraean Sea
Delhi-Topra pillar edict No. 7 of Ashoka

questions.question: In which century does the session date the Delhi-Topra pillar edict No. 7?
questions.explanation: The edict dates to the 3rd century BCE, in Ashoka's reign.

questions.question: The rise of what also saw the development of trading infrastructure, according to the session?
questions.explanation: The rise of the 16 Mahajanapadas saw trading infrastructure develop.

questions.question: What logistic support did caravanserais give traders? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Caravanserais gave security, shelter, food, water and other services.

questions.question: During the Mauryan period, trade routes extended into Southeast Asia through the:
questions.explanation: Mauryan routes extended through the Malay Peninsula into Southeast Asia.

questions.question: Which pass acted as a strategically important gateway on the Silk Road link to the subcontinent?
questions.explanation: The Khyber Pass was the strategic gateway for trade and communication.

questions.question: Which items are named among key exports in the session? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Exports included silk, cotton and muslin textiles, spices, gems, ivory, timber, bamboo, dyes, wootz steel and medicinal substances.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as an import of the caravan period?
questions.explanation: Imports listed were lead, wine, horses, crude glass, asphalt and antimony. Spices were exports.

questions.question: Wine, horses and crude glass are named among the exports of the caravan period.
questions.explanation: False. Wine, horses, crude glass, lead, asphalt and antimony are listed as imports.

questions.question: A caravan crossing a dry stretch reaches a roadside inn with a well and a fortified wall. Which feature of caravan trade does this illustrate?
questions.explanation: Inns or serais, wells and fortified outposts supplied security, water and shelter.
options: A Harappan coastal dock with processing centres for shell
Caravan infrastructure such as serais, wells and fortified outposts
A Roman sailing guide describing ports and seasons to sail
A Chola naval station supplying ships on the Bay of Bengal

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Caravanserais helped long-distance overland trade.
Reason (R): They provided security, shelter, food and water along the routes.
questions.explanation: Both are true and the second explains how they helped.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

questions.question: The earliest reference to a caravanserai is in the Delhi-______ pillar edict No. 7.
questions.explanation: The earliest Indian reference to a caravanserai is the Delhi-Topra pillar edict No. 7.

questions.question: Which are the two major trade routes named in the session's account of inland routes?
questions.explanation: The two major trade routes were the Uttarapatha and the Dakshinapatha.

questions.question: The term Uttarapatha is mentioned primarily in:
questions.explanation: The session says Uttarapatha is mentioned primarily in Panini's Ashtadhyayi.

questions.question: The session describes the Uttarapatha as a trans-regional route that is best seen as a:
questions.explanation: The Uttarapatha is described as a land-river route from north-west India across the Indo-Gangetic plains.

questions.question: The Uttarapatha ran from north-west India across the Indo-Gangetic plains up to the port of:
questions.explanation: The Uttarapatha reached Tamralipti on the Bay of Bengal.
options: Tamralipti on the Bay of Bengal

questions.question: Which places are named on the northern path of the Uttarapatha? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: The northern path included Lahore, Jalandhar, Saharanpur, Bijnor, Gorakhpur, Bihar and Bengal.

questions.question: Which places are named on the southern path? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: The southern path included Lahore, Indraprastha, Hastinapur, Varanasi, Prayagraj, Pataliputra and Rajgir.

questions.question: Which trade centres are named among India's most important in the session?
questions.explanation: The list includes Barygaza, Ujjaini, Muziris, Soppara, Pataliputra, Kalyana, Poduca, Kaveripattinam and Tamralipti.
options: Rome, Alexandria, Antioch, Damascus and Aden
Kashgar, Yarkand, Khotan, Bactria and Chang'an
Barygaza, Ujjaini, Muziris, Pataliputra and Tamralipti
Oman, Bahrain, Muscat, Aden and Zanzibar

questions.question: The Dakshinapatha stretched from Pataliputra in Magadha to:
questions.explanation: The Dakshinapatha ran from Pataliputra to Pratishthana (Paithan).

questions.question: Branch routes connected the Dakshinapatha to Virampattinam (Arikamedu) through:
questions.explanation: The Dakshinapatha was connected to Virampattinam or Arikamedu via Pratishthana.

questions.question: Which coasts were linked to the Uttarapatha by branch routes?
questions.explanation: The Uttarapatha was connected to the Sind and Odisha coasts.

questions.question: Which goods moved along the Uttarapatha? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Goods included lapis lazuli, silver and semi-precious stones from Afghanistan and Central Asia, and sea shells from the east coast.
options: Sea shells from the east coast

questions.question: Which items did mineral-rich Rajasthan supply along the Dakshinapatha? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Rajasthan supplied semi-precious stones, silver, gold, lead, copper, iron, sandalwood and hides.

questions.question: Which centres are named as important on the Dakshinapatha?
questions.explanation: Ujjain, Vidisha and Kaushambi were important trading centres on the Dakshinapatha.

questions.question: Lapis lazuli travelled along the Uttarapatha from Rajasthan.
questions.explanation: False. Lapis lazuli and other goods on the Uttarapatha came from Afghanistan and Central Asia; Rajasthan supplied materials along the Dakshinapatha.

questions.question: A trader at Pataliputra sends goods towards the Deccan and then to Arikamedu. Which route does the session describe?
questions.explanation: The Dakshinapatha ran from Pataliputra to Pratishthana, with a branch to Virampattinam (Arikamedu).
options: The Uttarapatha northwards through Taxila to the Oxus and Balkh
The Harappan Cholistan route between Punjab and Rajasthan
The Silk Road branch from Yarkand across the Karakoram to Leh
The Dakshinapatha with a branch via Pratishthana to Arikamedu

questions.question: How do the Uttarapatha and Dakshinapatha differ in the session?
questions.explanation: The Uttarapatha was the northern land-river route; the Dakshinapatha ran southwards to Pratishthana.
options: Uttarapatha crossed the north to Tamralipti and the north-west; Dakshinapatha ran from Pataliputra to Pratishthana
Uttarapatha was only a sea route to Arabia; Dakshinapatha was only a river in the Deccan
Both routes started at Tamralipti and ended together at the port of Arikamedu
Dakshinapatha is the overland Silk Road; Uttarapatha is the Indian Ocean spice route

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The Uttarapatha was connected to the Sind and Odisha coasts by branch routes.
Reason (R): The Dakshinapatha was connected to Virampattinam (Arikamedu) through Pratishthana.
questions.explanation: Both are true, but R is a separate example (the southern route) and does not explain A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

questions.question: According to the session, Chiang Kien's expedition led China to discover Europe and marked the birth of the Silk Road.
questions.explanation: True. The expedition led China to discover Europe and the birth of the Silk Road.

questions.question: Which statement about the inland routes is NOT supported by the session?
questions.explanation: The Uttarapatha began at the eastern end, Tamralipti; Pratishthana belongs to the Dakshinapatha.
options: The Uttarapatha was mentioned in Panini's Ashtadhyayi
The Dakshinapatha linked Pataliputra and Pratishthana
Branch routes joined both highways to ports

questions.question: Roughly how long was the Silk Road according to the session?
questions.explanation: The Silk Road spanned almost 7,000 miles from China through Central Asia, northern India and the Parthian Empire to Rome.

questions.question: Who first used the term Silk Road in 1838?
questions.explanation: German geographer Carl Ritter first used the term in 1838; it was popularised by von Richthofen in 1877.

questions.question: Who popularised the term Silk Road in 1877?
questions.explanation: Baron Ferdinand von Richthofen popularised the term in 1877.

questions.question: Chiang Kien was sent west in 138 BC by:
questions.explanation: The Chinese diplomat Chiang Kien was sent by Emperor Wu-ti in 138 BC.

questions.question: Chiang Kien returned to the Han capital Changan after three years.
questions.explanation: False. He returned after thirteen years, having been sent west in 138 BC with a caravan of one hundred men.

questions.question: With how many men was Chiang Kien's caravan sent west?
questions.explanation: He left with a caravan of one hundred men.

questions.question: The Silk Road, according to the session, is best understood as:
questions.explanation: It was not a single road but a series of caravan routes and trading posts across Eurasia.
options: One paved highway running straight from China to Rome
A single sea lane between the Red Sea and the Bay of Bengal
A canal system linking the Oxus river with the Ganga river
A network of caravan routes, trails, trading posts and oases

questions.question: The eastern terminus of the Silk Road was:
questions.explanation: The eastern terminus was the Chinese capital Chang'an, today's Xian.

questions.question: Which cities are named as western terminals? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: The western terminals included Byzantium or Constantinople, Antioch and Damascus.

questions.question: Which art tradition fused Indian Buddhist art under the Kushanas with Greek art introduced by Alexander?
questions.explanation: Gandharan art, in the Peshawar valley, fused Indian Buddhist and Greek art, with some Persian elements.

questions.question: The Mahabharata and the Arthashastra refer to China as:
questions.explanation: Both texts refer to China as Tsin.

questions.question: Which goods moved from China along the Silk Road? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: From China came silk, medical herbs, carved jade, furs and ceramics.

questions.question: Which goods were imported into China? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: China imported horses, glassware, raw jade, gold and silver.

questions.question: An important branch route leaving the southern Silk Road at Yarkand crossed the Karakoram to reach:
questions.explanation: The branch crossed the Karakoram passes to Leh and Srinagar and then reached north-west India.

questions.question: Chiang Kien's report also describes India's trade with south-western China through:
questions.explanation: His report deals with trade through Assam and Burma as early as the 2nd century BC.

questions.question: A scholar wants early Indian literary evidence of Chinese silk. Which sources does the session name?
questions.explanation: Silk is mentioned as a foreign gift in the epics and the Manusmriti; Kautilya mentions China silk; Kalidasa speaks of Chinanashuka.
options: Only Roman writers describing silk bought at Barygaza
The epics, the Manusmriti, Kautilya and Kalidasa's Abhigyan Shakuntalam
Only Chinese chronicles describing gifts sent to India
Only the Periplus and the inscriptions at Ban Don Ta Phet

questions.question: How does Xuanzang's role differ from Chiang Kien's in the session?
questions.explanation: Chiang Kien's expedition led China to discover Europe; Xuanzang travelled from China to India via the Silk Road and recorded Gandhara.
options: Xuanzang founded the Han dynasty; Chiang Kien wrote the text called Arthashastra
Chiang Kien reported on the west for the Han emperor; Xuanzang travelled to India and recorded Gandhara
Both men were Roman ambassadors who travelled from Rome to Pataliputra
Chiang Kien recorded Gandhara for Kanishka; Xuanzang coined the term Silk Road

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The Silk Road is not a single clearly defined road.
Reason (R): It is a series of caravan routes with trading posts, oases and emporia across Eurasia.
questions.explanation: Both are true and the second explains the first.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

questions.question: Kushan sites at Harwan, Ushkur and Kanispur show the diffusion of Silk Route art into Kashmir.
questions.explanation: True. Excavations there revealed the diffusion of art from different areas of the Silk Route.

questions.question: The Han dynasty (202 BC-220 AD) is associated with the rise and development of the ______ Road.
questions.explanation: The Han dynasty largely came to be associated with the Silk Road.

cards.back: About 7,000 miles; a network of routes; eastern terminus Chang'an (Xian); western terminals Byzantium/Constantinople, Antioch, Damascus.
Uttarapatha (north-west India across the Indo-Gangetic plains to Tamralipti) and Dakshinapatha (Pataliputra to Pratishthana).
Inns or serais, wells and fortified outposts, giving security, shelter, food and water.
Shell, copper, gold, lead, zinc, alabaster, limestone, steatite, and semi-precious stones (carnelian, agate, jasper).
Anuradhapura Brahmi script; Tamralipti and Bengal inscriptions; Kharoshti-Brahmi finds in Southeast Asia; Rouletted ware; Ban Don Ta Phet.
